result:
None of the three solutions has the correct final answer. Solutions 1 and 2 misuse the Sawayama–Thébault theorem, and Solution 3 asserts a relation it never derives, which a numerical check contradicts. Numerically the inradii come out near 5.48 and 6.24 for the two roots, so the sum is about 11.7, not any of the three offered values.

**The common setup is correct.** With D at the origin and BC on the x-axis, the centers are O₂ = (−5t, 5) and O₃ = (7/t, 7), where t = tan(∠ADC/2). The condition |O₂O₃| = 13 gives 5t + 7/t = √165, so t = (√165 ± 5)/10.

**Solutions 1 and 2 misstate the theorem.** The Sawayama–Thébault theorem says the incenter I lies on line O₂O₃. It does not say the incircle is tangent to ω₂ and ω₃. Solution 1 builds its equations on |IO₂| = ρ + 5 and |IO₃| = ρ + 7, and Solution 2 builds its cases on |O₂I| = r ± 5. Both rest on the false tangency claim, so 495/2 and 13 are unfounded.

**Solution 3 asserts an unproved relation.** It claims 1/r = ½(1/r₂ + 1/r₃) with no derivation, going from "the system reduces to" straight to the formula.

**Numerical check.** For each root of t, I solved the circumcircle tangency conditions. These conditions form a one-parameter family of triangles, and I tested one member for each root.

- For t ≈ 1.7845, I got a triangle with area ≈ 198.7 and s ≈ 36.28, so r ≈ 5.48. I checked that I lies on line O₂O₃.
- For t ≈ 0.7845, I got a triangle with r ≈ 6.24.

I did not confirm that r is constant across each family, and the triangles I tested were not acute. Even so, the two roots give different inradii, so r = 35/6 ≈ 5.83 cannot be the sum for either. The values 13 and 495/2 are also far from 11.7.

CHOICE: NONE
